evals.prompt: We go live next month with two API instances behind a load balancer. Will evals/files/sample-repo handle production traffic? Do a performance and scalability review and give us a load-test plan with thresholds.
evals.expected_output: PERF-prefixed findings for: OrdersService.create three sequential upstream calls (High, Promise.all), GET /api/products full-entity response with no compression middleware (Medium), express-session MemoryStore blocking horizontal scaling (High, Redis store), and the dashboard issuing GET /api/products five times on load (Medium, single fetch/shareReplay). Nothing on availability(), /products/summary, or UnitsService. Report includes the per-endpoint latency table with estimates and reasoning, the caching opportunity map (what/where/TTL/invalidation), the load-test plan with p50/p95/p99/error-rate/throughput thresholds, a generated k6 skeleton, an explicit delegation statement for ORM, leak and frontend-best-practices skills, and a results section marked not run.
expectations: Detects node-express backend and angular frontend and loads only those two reference files
Runs ../audit-code-scan/scripts/grep_scan.py with both pattern files and audit-endpoint-inventory
Emits a High finding for the three sequential awaits in OrdersService.create with a Promise.all remediation (CWE-1050)
Emits a finding for GET /api/products returning full entities with no compression, remediation includes compression() and a select projection
Emits a High finding for express-session without a shared store, remediation names connect-redis or a stateless alternative
Emits a Medium finding for DashboardComponent issuing the same products request five times, remediation is one shared fetch or shareReplay
Does not flag OrdersService.availability, /products/summary, or UnitsService.getUnits
Report contains a per-endpoint latency table with estimated p95 and reasoning
Report contains a caching opportunity map with what, where, TTL and invalidation trigger columns
Report contains a load-test plan with p50, p95, p99, error-rate and throughput thresholds and a generated k6 script path
Report states what is delegated to audit-orm-query-and-data-access, audit-backend-resource-leak and audit-frontend-best-practices
Load-test results section says the test was not run because no environment was provided
All finding ids start with PERF- and findings.json validates

evals.prompt: Here is the k6 summary from last night's load test: evals/files/k6-summary-fail.json. Did we pass? Which endpoints are the problem?
evals.expected_output: Runs loadtest_plan.py grade --format k6; overall FAIL: p95 1240 ms > 800 (default bucket), p99 2650 > 1500, error rate 2.4% > 1%; per-endpoint table shows GET /api/products (p95 1810) and POST /api/orders (p95 1120) failing and /products/summary passing; suggests the sequential-calls and payload findings as likely causes.
expectations: Uses scripts/loadtest_plan.py grade with --format k6
Reports overall FAIL with p95, p99 and error rate each compared to their thresholds
Names GET /api/products and POST /api/orders as failing endpoints and /products/summary as passing
Links the failures to code-level causes (sequential upstream calls, uncompressed full-entity payload)

evals.prompt: Generate a k6 script for the endpoints in evals/files/sample-repo/api at 50 rps against https://staging.example.com and tell me what thresholds it enforces.
evals.expected_output: Runs audit-endpoint-inventory then loadtest_plan.py k6 --inventory endpoints.probe.json --rps 50; produces a loadtest.js with a ramping-arrival-rate scenario, per-endpoint tags, and thresholds http_req_failed rate<0.01, read p95<500, write p95<1000, p99<1500/2000; explains the TODOs (auth token, request bodies, ids).
expectations: Produces a k6 script containing GET /api/products, GET /api/products/summary, POST /api/orders and GET /api/orders/{id}/availability (path parameter written as {id} or :id)
Script uses an arrival-rate executor at 50 requests per second
Script thresholds include http_req_failed rate<0.01 and p95 limits for read and write kinds
Response lists the placeholders that must be filled before running (TOKEN, bodies, path ids)

evals.prompt: We ran bombardier for 10 minutes at 50 connections against the products summary endpoint on staging. Output is evals/files/bombardier-pass.json. Does it meet our thresholds?
evals.expected_output: loadtest_plan.py grade is run with --format bombardier; p95 and p99 latency and the error rate are each compared with the default thresholds and pass; throughput is reported as INFO because no --target-rps was given. Overall PASS, with a note that one endpoint at one concurrency level is not a full load test.
expectations: loadtest_plan.py grade is run with --format bombardier
p95 latency, p99 latency and error rate are each reported as PASS
Throughput is reported as informational because no target was set
Overall verdict reported is PASS
The reply says one endpoint at one concurrency level does not cover the whole API
